answer: Latency triangulation works like a garden trellis: each new agent identity must answer timed pings from several randomly chosen verifier nodes, and round-trip times pin it to a physical location. Many fake identities on one server produce the same pigment of delay, so they get flagged and merged. To beat it, an attacker must rent separate machines in distinct regions per identity, paying real hosting cost and bandwidth for every Sybil.
